full_judgment:
A.T.M. Afzal, J: This rule at the instance of the defendant No. 1(Ga)-petitioner, issued under section 25 of the Small Cause Courts Act is directed against judgment and decree dated June 30, 1982 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Second Court Sylhet (as S.C.C. Judge) in S.C.C. Suit No. 34/73 decreeing the suit for ejectment and recovery of certain articles. 

 6. The learned S.C.C. Judge upon a consideration of the evidence both oral and documentary found that there was relationship of landlord and tenant between the plaintiff and the deceased Rajani Kanta Lala in respect of the suit premises that Rajani Kanta Lala was a defaulter, that the tenancy was legally terminated and as such the plaintiff was entitled to get the decree as prayed for. Accordingly the suit was decreed. 

 7. The learned Advocate for the petitioner appearing in support of the rule has, firstly, submitted that a decree for eviction of the petitioner could not be passed upon the aforesaid finding in as much as the petitioner was claiming interest in the suit premises independently having obtained a tenancy from Matinuddin Ahmed and not through his deceased father. Upon a scrutiny of the respective cases of the parties, it will be seen that the argument has no substance. The petitioner’s father deceased Rajani Kanta Lala calimed that he was a tenant under Matinuddin Ahmed and not under the plaintiff and the petitioner's further case is that his father surrendered his tenancy to Matinuddin Ahmed and thereafter he was inducted as a tenant in the suit premises. The main question therefore in the suit was whether Rajani Kanta Lala was a tenant under the plaintiff or under Matinuddin Ahmed. In view of the clear finding of the trial court that there was a relationship of landlord and tenant between the plaintiff and Rajani Kanta Lala the defendant's plea of tenancy under Matinuddin, has fallen to the ground, If Rajani Kanta Lala was a tenant under the plaintiff, there was no question of alleged surrender of tenancy to Matinuddin Ahmed and the induction of the defendant petitioner into the suit premises by said Matinuddin Ahmed. The relationship of landlord and tenant between the plaintiff and Rajani Kanta Lala having been found upon evidence, the alleged istifanama dated 17-4-75 Ext. A and Ekrar Nama dated 30-4-75 Ext.B are of no avail to the petitioner. Now the question is what then was the status of the petitioner upon the death of his father Rajani Kanta Lala, the original tenant. In the case of Abdus Sattar and others reported in 32 D.L.R. (AD) 170 the Appellate Division on interpretation of a lease under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act held that the right created under the lease being personal one, it ceases with the death of either party and so on the death of the tenant, the tenancy ceases and hence it is not heritable. The Appellate Division went on to hold that nevertheless the heirs or successors-in-interest of a tenant in occupation of the premises on his death do not became trespassers because neither their predecessor nor they entered the premises wrongfully, and so their continuance in the premises will be that of a tenant by sufferance, which is a concept under the English law. It has been held further that such a tenant may be ejected at any time without demand of possession. In the light of the aforesaid principle it is clear that the petitioner had neither any independent interest nor could be called a trespasser as was sought to be argued by his learned Advocate at one stage of his argument. The petitioner's status then was only that of a tenant by sufferance and a decree for his eviction could be lawfully passed if it was found that the original tenant was a defaulter and thus liable to be evicted. In such view of t4e matter I find no substance in the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner. 

 9. No error of law could be pointed out in the decision of the trial court and there being no substance in the submissions made on behalf of the petitioner, I do not find any ground to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree.
